items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
RZ05/24 Public Meeting Information Report - 6235 Guelph Street (Aypa
notes: Power Battery Energy Storage System Facility).

Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on the subject land known as 6235 Guelph Street, former Nichol Township.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from ‘A.19.3’ (Agricultural Exception) and ‘EP’ (Environmental Protection) to ‘A.19.X’ (Agricultural Exception) and ‘EP’ (Environmental Protection). The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to permit a battery energy storage facility on a portion of the property (subject land).

He indicated the purpose of the proposed County of Wellington Official Plan Amendment is to amend Schedule B1 (Centre Wellington) by adding a site specific policy on a portion of the land described as Lot 11, Concession 3, in the Township of Centre Wellington from “Prime Agricultural” to “Prime Agricultural Special” to permit a battery energy storage facility.

He indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting, if one is held, or make written submissions to The Corporation of the County of Wellington in respect of the proposed official plan amendment before the approval authority gives or refuses to give approval to the proposed official plan amendment, or if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of The Corporation of the County of Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to The Corporation of the County of Wellington before the proposed official plan amendment is adopted, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision of The Corporation of the County of Wellington to the OLT.

Mayor Watters advised if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting, if one is held, or make written submissions to The Corporation of the County of Wellington in respect of the proposed official plan amendment before the approval authority gives or refuses to give approval to the official plan amendment, or if a person or public body does not make oral submissions to The Corporation of the County of Wellington before the proposed official plan amendment is adopted, the person or public body may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters stated if anyone wishes to be notified of the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington in respect of the proposed zoning by- law amendment, a written request must be filed with the Clerk of the Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, Ontario, N0B 1S0.

Any person or public body may appeal a decision of The County of Wellington not later than 20 days after the day that the giving or written notice had been completed. If anyone wishes to be notified of the decision of The Corporation of the County of Wellington in respect of this proposed County Official Plan amendment, a written request must be filed with the Director of Planning and Development, Corporation of the County of Wellington, 74 Woolwich Street, Guelph, Ontario, N1H 3T9

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before October 31, 2024. A copy was also placed in the Wellington Advertiser on October 31, 2024. She confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on October 31, 2024.
Mayor Watters asked Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services to introduce the application.

M. Iglesias indicated the property is the subject of a County Official Plan Amendment application (OP 2024-04) and Township Zoning By-law Amendment application (RZ05/24) to facilitate the installation of an independently operated Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) on a portion of the property. She explained the entire property is approximately 43 ha and is located at the southeast corner of Guelph Street and Second Line. It is surrounded by future development lands related to the South Fergus Secondary Plan Area, a landscaping business to the east, and agricultural lands to the west and south. The property is actively farmed and contains two dwellings and farm buildings accessed from Guelph Street. M. Iglesias further explained only a portion of the property, approximately 6 hectares would be leased to the applicant and would be subject to the amendments. The applicant is seeking to add site specific provisions to the property to allow the BESS, but the site would remain Prime Agricultural.
She indicated the site plan approval process would address design details such as lighting, landscaping, grading/servicing, fire safety and agricultural restoration.
Mayor Watters asked Pierre Chauvin, MHBC on behalf of Aypa Power to make a presentation. The consultant team consisted of the following:
Ondrej Benjik, Director, Business Development, Leslie Greener, Stantec, Chief Brian Fink, Fire & Risk Alliance and Nadia Pabst, Aypa Power, Vice President, Government & Regulatory Affairs.

P. Chauvin indicated the Independent Electricity System Operator (IESO) is a Crown Corporation that manages Ontario’s power system and plans for future capacity that is procuring solutions to support the grid reliability, including storage facilities through Long Term Procurements. The Elora BESS is part of a Long-Term Procurement project, planning to connect to the existing transmission line that bisects the subject property. They will receive electricity from the power grid and store it, re-injecting the energy when needed.

He provided site context, outlined the scope of the development, the key benefits to the Township and the various studies undertaken and completed. P. Chauvin outlined the land stewardship and site restoration goals, the design to incorporate vegetation and screening and the fire safety strategy.
Delegations:

a) Anthea Millikin, resident, expressed concerns with respect to fire safety, and the impact of the development on the groundwater and soil in the event of a fire. She questioned if a fire safety and evacuation plan has been developed and suggested the municipality collect monetary security in the event of a fire.

b) Donna McCaw, on behalf of Save Our Water, emphasized the large scale of the proposal and the potential dangers, including fire, pollution, and contamination. D. McCaw suggested Council consider either reducing the size of the facility or indicate Centre Wellington is not a willing host.

c) Janet Harrop, on behalf of Wellington Federation of Agriculture, provided an overview of the membership and the advocacy role to support the protection and preservation of agricultural land for the purpose of growing, harvesting and producing food. She indicated the Federation recognizes the Provincial Policy Statement permits energy storage systems as on-farm diversified uses (OFDU) in prime agricultural areas, limited to 2% or 1 hectare to provide additional revenue streams for farmers and remain a secondary use on the site. J.

Harrop expressed concerns regarding the impact the proposal will have on existing municipal drains, water, disruption of the soil, and the restoration of the site, given it is prime agricultural land. She indicated the Federation opposes the rezoning application and encouraged further investigation to find a more suitable site.

Mayor Watters asked if there was anyone in the audience wishing to speak to the application. There being none, Mayor Watters offered the applicant or staff an opportunity to respond to comments/questions raised by the delegations.
There being none, Mayor Watters offered Council an opportunity to ask any questions of the applicant or staff.

Ondrej Benjik, Director, Business Development, Leslie Greener, Stantec, Chief Brian Fink, Fire & Risk Alliance and Nadia Pabst, Aypa Power, Vice President, Government & Regulatory Affairs responded to questions related to the benefits of the proposal for Centre Wellington, noise impact on future residential development, potential for fires and the emergency response preparedness, air pollution monitoring, restoration strategy and the rationale for the 400 mega watt size of the facility.
Fire Chief Tom Mulvey responded to questions regarding Centre Wellington’s training and ability to respond to an emergency.
Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services responded to questions regarding future reconstruction of 2nd Line to accommodate residential development.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the by-law at a future Council meeting.
Mayor Watters declared the meeting adjourned and called for a 7 minute recess. The meeting resumed at 8:08 pm.

items.title: Kathryn Giffen, Board Co-Chair, Elora Centre for the Arts appeared
notes: before Council regarding agenda item re: 12.4 Community Investment Fund Policy. She expressed concerns with the restructuring of the funding streams to remove the capital stream. She highlighted the great work accomplished in the past to address maintenance improvements, noting the gratitude of the Centre for the various levels of support. K.
Griffen requested the capital funding not be removed from the Community Investment Fund Policy and that consideration be given to streamlining and simplifying the funding criteria.

In response to a question from Councillor Wilton, Molly Kleiker, Director of Development indicated the Centre has received approximately $700,000 over the years in capital funding, including the funding received through the Jack R MacDonald fund.

Mayor Watters indicated he was unaware of the delegation’s subject matter, so he wished to declare a conflict of interest due to his relationship with Riverfest and their affiliation with the Elora Centre for the Arts.
